preseason_hypothesis: Brown is the offense's defined alpha WR1 and clear target leader
confirming_evidence: leads receiver targets; first-read and red-zone looks; every-down snaps. WEEK 1 PARTIAL SUPPORT (2026-09-10): restricted to the 31 snaps Brown played before his Q3 injury, he led the team with 4 targets to Douglas's 3, about a 31% share of the 13 targets thrown in that window, and led in receptions and yards at his exit.
disconfirming_evidence: distributed targets deny him a clear lead; slow scheme fit. NOTE: Brown's full-game fourth-place target finish (4, behind Douglas 7, Stevenson 6, Hollins 5) is an ARTEFACT of his absence for the final 24 minutes and is NOT disconfirming evidence.
review_trigger: first two regular-season games IN WHICH BROWN PLAYS A FULL GAME. Week 1 does not count toward the trigger: he played 44% of snaps (31 of 71) and was ruled out during Q3. Availability-blocked pending his Week 2 status, which is unknown.

preseason_hypothesis: New England concentrates targets around Brown rather than spreading them
confirming_evidence: a defined top target with clear route/first-read priority. Week 1 measured targets: Douglas 7, Stevenson 6, Hollins 5, Brown 4, Henry 3, Doubs 3, Larison 2, Raridon 1, on a 31-target denominator. IN-WINDOW SPLIT: over the 13 targets thrown while Brown was on the field, Brown led with 4, Douglas 3, Henry 2, and Stevenson/Hollins/Larison/Raridon 1 each. Doubs drew 0. The offense concentrated on Brown when he was available.
disconfirming_evidence: even distribution across Brown, Doubs, slot, and tight end. Week 1 reads as distributed, but the sample is CONTAMINATED: Brown led targets while on the field and missed the final 24 minutes. Do not score this hypothesis on the full-game table.
review_trigger: first four regular-season games; Week 1 admitted only with the Brown-availability caveat recorded

preseason_hypothesis: Boutte was traded to Houston and no longer has a New England role
disconfirming_evidence: trade voided or Boutte returns to New England

preseason_hypothesis: Doubs opens as a stable complementary starter opposite Brown
confirming_evidence: first-unit snaps; steady targets. Week 1: Doubs played 40 of 71 snaps (56%), THIRD among receivers behind Hollins (50) and Douglas (44).
disconfirming_evidence: loses outside snaps to Kyle Williams or another younger receiver. WEEK 1 CHALLENGES THIS: 3 targets and ZERO receptions, the weakest measured line of any regular. COMPETING EXPLANATION RETAINED: Kyed reports Hollins was used heavily on run plays in the first half, suppressing Doubs and Douglas snaps for a reason unrelated to standing. Not recorded as a demotion. IN-WINDOW REFINEMENT (verified 2026-09-10 from the official play-by-play): Doubs drew ZERO targets while A.J. Brown was on the field. All three of his targets came AFTER Brown's Q3 exit, and the first of them was intercepted by Pritchett and returned 30 yards. His Week 1 low is therefore NOT a post-Brown artefact — it happened while the offense was whole, which is stronger evidence than the full-game line alone suggests.
review_trigger: Week 2 snap share and receptions, read against Brown's availability: if Brown misses time, Doubs's opportunity rises even as his Week 1 measurement fell. These point in opposite directions and must be assessed together.

preseason_hypothesis: Henry retains a steady middle-field and red-zone tight-end role
confirming_evidence: routes on a majority of dropbacks; red-zone targets. Week 1: Henry played 54 of 71 snaps (76%), second among pass catchers, with 3 receptions on 3 targets for 26 yards.
disconfirming_evidence: rookie Raridon or receivers absorb tight-end targets. Week 1 partial signal: Raridon played 38 snaps (54%) and caught the team's ONLY touchdown, a 2-yard score on New England's single goal-to-go snap. One target is not target absorption.
review_trigger: first two regular-season games. Week 1 supports the snap-share half and is silent on the red-zone half: only one inside-5 snap existed all game.

preseason_hypothesis: Stevenson opens as the lead early-down and short-yardage back
confirming_evidence: first-unit carries; goal-line work. WEEK 1 MEASURED (Henderson absent): 60 of 71 snaps (85%), 18 of 31 carries (58%), 6 of 31 targets, and on the field for ALL 11 two-minute snaps across both halves. Kiner took 8 snaps and 6 carries, all on first or second down; Larison took 3 snaps and ZERO carries.
disconfirming_evidence: Henderson takes a three-down role; committee by series. Week 1 supplies NO evidence either way: Henderson was an official inactive.
review_trigger: First two regular-season games in which BOTH Stevenson and Henderson are available. Week 1 documents Henderson-absent usage only and does not count. GOAL-LINE REMAINS UNRESOLVED: New England ran exactly one snap inside the Seattle 5 all game (a touchdown pass), so n=1 and no back's goal-line role was tested.

preseason_hypothesis: Henderson wins the passing-down and explosive-play role and pushes for a larger share
confirming_evidence: routes and targets; passing-down snaps; goal-line involvement
disconfirming_evidence: limited to change-of-pace; low route share. Week 1 supplies NO evidence: Henderson was inactive. Stevenson's 85% snap share and two-minute role were earned in Henderson's absence and cannot disconfirm Henderson's healthy role.
review_trigger: First two regular-season games after Henderson is available; Week 1 absence cannot disconfirm the healthy role hypothesis and does not count toward the trigger. NEXT CHECK: Henderson's Week 2 practice participation, which no registered source established as of 2026-09-10.

preseason_hypothesis: Maye takes another step with an upgraded supporting cast
confirming_evidence: efficient production; sustained drives; touchdown rate rises
disconfirming_evidence: stalled development; pressure or turnover issues. WEEK 1 CHALLENGES THIS: Maye threw 3 interceptions on 33 attempts for a 54.9 passer rating, with 178 gross passing yards. New England out-gained Seattle and held the ball 34:17 and still lost; the game ended on an interception at the Seattle 16 with 26 seconds left and New England in range to win. He also rushed 7 times for 47 yards.
review_trigger: first four regular-season games. One game is not a trend, but the turnover mechanism is the specific thing to watch and it is the mechanism that decided this game.

preseason_hypothesis: The interior line and tackle spot stabilize after the Bradbury trade and Vera-Tucker/Lomu additions
confirming_evidence: stable first-unit five; clean protection; official 2026-08-30 roster analysis lists the starting five as Campbell (LT), Vera-Tucker (LG), Jared Wilson (C), Onwenu (RG), Moses (RT), set before camp; team site reports the starting five intact for Week 1
disconfirming_evidence: rotating interior; center or tackle instability; rising pressure. WEEK 1: 3 sacks allowed for 10 yards. Lazar's film charting puts the pressure rate at 38.1% (revised up from 28.6% on initial viewing) with 4 hurries charged to Vera-Tucker; Kyed INDEPENDENTLY calls Vera-Tucker the line's weak link with multiple hurries. Two organizationally independent origins agree, which is genuine corroboration rather than recirculation.
review_trigger: first two regular-season games with protection charting. Week 1 supplies one game. NOTE ON SOURCING: Lazar is team-employed; Kyed's independent assessment is the only non-club check in the Week 1 batch and it agrees.
